title: Рік без матері: про що мріє забути та як сумує 15-річна донька найстаршої породіллі України Підвербна
content_c:
Рік без матері: про що мріє забути та як сумує 15-річна донька найстаршої породіллі України Підвербна
У родині та оточенні доньки найстаршої породіллі України Анни Підвербної розповіли, як склалась її доля та чим займається зараз ця дівчина.
Днями мине рік, як донька найстаршої породіллі України, 15-річна чернігівчанка Анна Підвербна, живе без рідної мами. На початку листопада 2025 року померла найстарша породілля нашої країни — 80-річна чернігівчанка Валентина Підвербна, яка народила доньку Анну у віці 65 років після процедури штучного запліднення. За ці 15 років в Україні старшої за Підвербну породіллі не з’явилося.
Донька Підвербної, Анна, якій у лютому виповниться 16 років, зараз, як відомо, мешкає зі своєю офіційною опікункою, чернігівчанкою Оленою Ятченко. Під час одного зі своїх останніх інтерв’ю для ТСН.ua безпосередньо Анна Підвербна висловила думку, що під час спільного проживання з мамою, крім позитивних моментів були такі, котрі хотілось би забути назавжди.
Подробиці того, як дитина прожила цей рік — це в коментарі для ТСН.ua розповіла її опікунка Олена Ятченко та чернігівська громадська діячка Оксана Тунік-Фриз, яка приймає участь у житті Анни Підвербної.
Олена Ятченко обережно каже, відповідаючи на питання ТСН.ua, що, враховуючи низку конфліктів, які у Ані були з Валентиною Підвербною, зараз дитині, звісно, легше.
«Їй легше. Конфліктів, звісно, немає, але час від часу Аня згадує маму та сумує. Згадує те, що було доброго та не дуже. Все, як у житті. Чи заздрить вона тим одноліткам, у яких є рідні мами — я цього не знаю», — відповіла нам опікунка Анни Підвербної.
На пряме питання про те, чи буває таке, що Аня плаче через те, що немає мами, Олена Ятченко відповіла так: «Ні. Просто сумує, знає, що її мамі було важко і що мама вже спочиває там… Сама Аня зараз навчається (здобуває музичну освіту), вчиться старанно, кожного ранку поспішає на навчання».
«Я вважаю, що у Ані є ефект пружини, яку довго тримали. Дитина зараз просто «вистрілила» і стала людиною з достатньо дорослим мисленням. У неї проявились здібності у багатьох напрямках. Можливо, через те, що вона була вимушена стати дорослою у свій час. Росте дуже цікава людина, у якої гарні здібності у навчанні, людина, яка у 15 років може серйозно дискутувати навіть на політичні теми, але при цьому залишається дитиною. Яка любить та пам’ятає свою маму, каже, що якби не мама, то і її не було би. Але і критично ставиться до всього того поганого, що довелось пережити у дитинстві. Разом з цим вона дуже вразлива. Її тригерить тема дітей, у яких немає батьків. У неї є плани допомагати таким діткам», — каже пані Оксана.
За її словами, нещодавно Аня у центрі міста перебувала недалеко від того місця, де стався приліт російського дрона. У той день у Чернігові внаслідок атаки РФ загинули дві 15-річні дівчини.
«Аня набрала мене, розповіла, що її „тіпає“ після того, що сталося. Потім перейшла до безпечного місця», — розповіла нам Оксана Тунік-Фриз.
Останнє побажання найстарішої породіллі Валентини Підвербної
За 8 тижнів до своєї смерті, у 20-х числах вересня 2025 року Валентина Підвербна погодилася дати інтерв’ю ТСН.ua. Під час спілкування вона плакала, але знайшла сили розповісти, що змогла зробити ремонт у квартирі, щоб покращити житлові умови заради можливого повернення доньки — або через суди, або коли Аня стане повнолітньою.
Але, за її словами, ремонт просувався дуже повільно через високу вартість будівельних матеріалів та меблів — на ці покупки Підвербна відкладала гроші з мізерної пенсії.
Намагаючись повернути дитину, Підвербна дійшла до висновку, що їй треба звертатись до президента України Володимира Зеленського. Вона тоді додала, що знаходила можливість приїхати до Києва. Утім, цього так і не сталося.
Історія родини Підвербних: що відомо
Про Аню Підвербну та її матір стало відомо в лютому 2011 року. Валентина Григорівна народила доньку у віці 65 років шляхом штучного запліднення.
Навесні 2023 року, коли Підвербній-молодшій було повних 12 років, спалахнув гучний скандал. У квітні дівчинка опублікувала в соцмережах низку дописів, в яких повідомила про те, що її мати, 78-річна Валентина Підвербна, начебто знущається з неї — дряпає, ображає, не дозволяє виконувати елементарні гігієнічні процедури.
Одразу після цього до квартири Підвербних приїхали правоохоронці, психологи, соцслужби. Дитина була вилучена і направлена до лікарні для обстеження, а згодом переведена до реабілітаційного центру.
Станом на зараз Аня Підвербна мешкає разом із своєю опікункою Оленою Ятченко.
За словами останньої, дитина має належні та комфортні умови проживання, певний час тому лікарі зробили Анні Підвербній операцію, щоб покращити зір, дитина закінчила школу та опановує музичну освіту.
Нагадаємо, раніше повідомлялось про те, що донька найстаршої породіллі Аня Підвербна приголомшила своїми зізнаннями. 15-річна донька найстаршої породіллі України Підвербної розповіла невідомі подробиці життя з 80-річною мамою та про те, за яких обставин перелякалась найбільше.

title: Умеров рассказал, о чем будут договариваться в Брюсселе
content_c:
Рустем Умеров сообщил о запланированных на 4–5 ноября переговорах в Брюсселе с участием представителей Украины, США и европейских партнеров.
По его словам, эти встречи станут продолжением переговоров, которые ранее состоялись во Флориде и Осло с целью достижения мира в Украине.
«Завтра и послезавтра вместе с командой и партнерами будем работать в Брюсселе. В повестке дня — работа над Prosperity Plan и гарантиями безопасности для Украины. Теперь на уровне рабочих групп мы детально проработаем наработки по послевоенному восстановлению, экономическому развитию и долгосрочной устойчивости Украины», — отметил Умеров.
Он добавил, что встречи будет принимать Европейская комиссия. В них примут участие представители США, Великобритании, Франции, Германии, НАТО и Всемирного банка. С украинской стороны к работе присоединятся команды Министерства экономики, Министерства финансов, Министерства обороны и Офиса президента.
В четверг, 5 ноября, также продолжатся консультации по вопросам гарантий безопасности для Украины с участием представителей США, Великобритании, Франции, Германии и НАТО.
«Безопасность, восстановление и развитие должны быть частями одного плана для Украины после войны», — подытожил Умеров.
В то же время 10–11 ноября ожидаются трехсторонние переговоры между Украиной, США и Россией в Абу-Даби (ОАЭ). О подготовке к ним ранее сообщил президент Владимир Зеленский.

title: Трамп заявив про готовність сторін до угоди щодо завершення війни, українські переговорники не поділяють оптимізму – ЗМІ
content_c:
Президент США Дональд Трамп висловив оптимістичну оцінку щодо перспективи російсько-українських мирних переговорів, заявивши про нібито готовність обох сторін конфлікту до досягнення домовленостей, однак українські представники заперечують такі висновки, повідомляє Clash Report із посиланням на Financial Times у середу.
"Я думаю, що вони обидва перебувають на тій стадії, коли кажуть: "Давайте укладемо угоду"", – зазначив Трамп в інтерв'ю газеті.
Водночас українські переговорники не поділяють подібного оптимізму щодо готовності Москви до реального врегулювання та продовження конструктивного діалогу на справедливих умовах.

title: Irish Olympian Ciara Mageean was a 'talented and inspirational human being'
content_c:
Olympian Ciara Mageean was a 'talented and inspirational human being'
- Published
Olympian Ciara Mageean has been described as a "truly remarkable, immensely talented and inspirational human being" in a tribute read out at her funeral.
Hundreds of people have paid their respects to the runner at her funeral on Tuesday.
The former European champion and two-time Olympic runner died on Sunday after she was diagnosed with stage four bowel cancer.
Among those in attendance at the funeral in Portaferry, County Down, were Northern Ireland First Minister Michelle O'Neill, as well as fellow Olympian Rhys McClenaghan and 1972 gold medallist Lady Mary Peters.
Mageean's funeral cortege was given a guard of honour by Portaferry GAC and her former school, Assumption Grammar in Ballynahinch.
Her death comes less than three weeks after her marriage to her long-term partner Thomas Moran.
Mourners began arriving at around midday for the 2:00 GMT requiem Mass at St Patrick's Church.
Family, friends and those wishing to pay their respects followed the funeral cortege the short distance along the Ballyphilip Road from Mageean's family home to the church.

Noticing blood in your poo - which may appear black or dark red in the toilet bowl - can be a sign of bowel cancer.

title: Car finance compensation payments explained
content_c:
Car finance compensation payments explained
- Published
Millions of drivers who were mis-sold car finance agreements must wait until at least 2027 to receive compensation, although some may be offered an early settlement.
Average payments of about £829 are expected under the rules published by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA).
However, legal challenges to the scheme - which will be heard in February 2027 -mean compensation calculations and payments have been delayed.
Who could receive car finance compensation?
The vast majority of new cars, and many second-hand ones, are bought with finance agreements. Customers pay an initial deposit to secure the vehicle, then a monthly fee with interest.
Compensation could be given to many of those who took out a car loan between April 2007 and November 2024.
The decision by the FCA, the financial regulator, applies to about 12 million car loans - about 37% of the total number during the period.
In 2021, the FCA banned deals where car dealers received commission from lenders, based on the interest rate charged to the customer. These were known as discretionary commission arrangements (DCAs) and customers were often not told about them.
The FCA said this provided an incentive for a buyer to be charged a higher-than-necessary interest rate, leaving them paying too much.
Other car buyers were also judged to have signed unfair contracts because the commission paid to the dealer was so high - accounting for 39% of the total cost of credit and 10% of the loan.
Some customers were not given accurate information about the best finance deal because of exclusive arrangements between car dealers and lenders.
How much compensation could victims receive?
Under the latest proposals, the FCA expects average payouts of £829 per mis-sold agreement.
The total cost of the compensation, including administrative costs, could hit £9.1bn.
How much individual consumers receive will depend on the degree of harm suffered.
The FCA has announced some claimants might be offered an early settlement, but only if it as good as what would be paid under the current proposed central scheme.
What do victims need to do to claim compensation?
Complaints have already been made about four million finance agreements. Those people do not need to do anything.
The regulator urged anyone who has not yet complained to contact their car loan provider directly, rather than using a third-party claims management company.
The regulator's central compensation scheme allows people to complain and potentially receive compensation for mis-sold deals without the need for a lawyer or to go through the courts.
Motorists have also been warned to be on the alert for scammers posing as car finance lenders offering fake compensation.
The FCA has published this guidance on how to complain, external.
Under its plans:
- lenders will respond to claims, explaining if you are owed compensation and how much – but timing of those letters is now uncertain owing to the legal challenge
- those who complain before the scheme gets up and running are likely to receive compensation faster
- some people who complained by 30 June and are not owed compensation should be told by 18 November, if the agreement began on or after 1 April 2014 and you complained by 30 June 2026
- some of those who complained by 31 August will be told if they are not owed compensation by 18 January 2027, if the agreement began before 1 April 2014
- there are exemptions, external, and anyone who does not hear from their lender by the dates set out, isn't necessarily owed compensation
- those who have not complained will be contacted by their lender. People will be asked if they want to opt in to the scheme to have their case reviewed
- those motor finance borrowers who do not receive a letter - for example because lenders no longer have their details and cannot trace them - can still make a claim
Regulators have warned claims management companies and law firms involved in motor finance commission claims to make sure consumers do not have multiple representatives for the same claim and are not charged excessive termination fees.
FCA boss Nikhil Rathi told the BBC's Today programme there are "many law firms out there who would like to get 30% of any compensation", stressing that the regulator's scheme was "free to use" for consumers.
When will drivers receive compensation and who will pay?
Millions of drivers were in line to receive compensation this year, and most of the remainder should have got compensation by the end of 2027.
But the FCA has confirmed that no compensation will be paid before 2027 as a result of legal challenges to the scheme.
Consumer Voice said the scheme left "too many people short-changed". The FCA has also received challenges from three lenders: Volkswagen Financial Services, Mercedes Benz Financial Services, and Credit Agricole Auto Finance.
The UK's Upper Tribunal has agreed to hear legal challenges to the scheme, with a hearing scheduled for 16 February to 3 March.
It means that lenders will no longer need to calculate or pay compensation to people owed money under its scheme, until the legal process concludes.
The FCA said it would need to decide what to do next if the courts decided to overturn the programme. Without a scheme in place, the FCA has estimated that up to 19 million complaints would need to be handled individually, taking three years and costing lenders £6bn more.
It said it would "defend the scheme robustly as lawful and the best way to resolve such a widespread, long running and complex issue".
Ultimately, the industry is expected to cover the full costs of any compensation scheme, including any administrative costs.
Lenders - including some of the UK's biggest banks and specialist motor finance firms - have already set aside billions of pounds for potential payouts.
Can drivers get an early settlement?
The FCA said a minority of claimants will be made early offers, but most will have to wait for the outcome of next year's court case.
With huge compensation payouts inevitable, Barclays will offer early settlements to some claimants, with others expected to follow suit.
The FCA has published a factsheet to help drivers, external work out whether they should accept early settlements from lenders.
Accepting would mean quicker payouts but remove them from any changes to the central scheme.
What's been the reaction to the payout plan?
The body that represents the lending industry, the Finance and Leasing Association, said it had "concerns" about the central programme but that it was choosing not to raise a legal challenge.
Santander, Barclays and Lloyds also accepted the scheme, despite raising concerns that the level of redress is disproportionate to those who suffered harm.
Even if drivers are entitled to compensation from these lenders they will need to wait.
There were some concessions made to lenders in a scaled-down final compensation plan from the FCA.
The Supreme Court considered three test cases which influenced the FCA's decision and, ultimately, limited how broad the compensation programme could have been.
It focused on whether the car dealers had a duty to act on behalf of their customers, rather than in their own interests. The test case which was upheld was that of Marcus Johnson, who bought his first car - a Suzuki Swift - in 2017.
In his case, the Supreme Court said the terms of his finance deal were unfair due of the size of the commission payment, and the fact he appeared to have been misled over the relationship between the finance firm and the dealer.
Get in touch
Have you been turned down for compensation relating to a car finance deal? Share your experiences.

title: Seven reported bomb threats against European flights confirmed as false alarms – as it happened
content_c:
At least seven flights and a cruise ship in Europe received bomb threats, causing disruption at airports although no devices were discovered. At least two flights to Warsaw, two to Sofia, two to Rome and one to Murcia airport in Spain were subjected to the threats on Tuesday and another flight to Sofia had been threatened a day earlier. 
An airport in Warsaw was briefly shut and the Italian Air Force accompanied one of the flights to Rome, while an Israel-bound cruise ship was searched for bombs in Greece.
Authorities diverted a LOT flight from London that was meant to land at Warsaw’s Chopin airport to nearby Modlin airport, which was closed and then reopened after the plane was searched and no device was found. Another Warsaw-bound flight, an SAS flight from Copenhagen, landed at Chopin as scheduled. Chopin airport said no device was found and the airport remained operational.
Bomb threats were made against planes traveling from Milan/Bergamo and Dublin to Sofia, Bulgaria’s transport ministry said in a statement to Reuters. Both landed safely and no explosive devices were found on inspection.
The Bergamo flight was operated by Wizz Air and was carrying 176 passengers, the statement said. The Dublin flight, operated by Ryanair, had 186 passengers on board. Bulgarian news agency BTA had earlier quoted an interior ministry official as saying a flight from Israel had been affected, but authorities later said this was not the case.
In Murcia in southeastern Spain, parts of an airport were cordoned off after a bomb threat was reported on a Ryanair flight from Manchester. Officials said the report proved to be a hoax, and the airport resumed normal operations after authorities found no explosives on board.
Two other Ryanair flights - one from Lisbon and another from Dublin - were searched at Rome’s Fiumicino airport following bomb threats, said a source from airport operator ADR. The Dublin flight was escorted by the Italian Air Force until it landed. The alert was cleared and the airport continued to operate as usual with no effects on other flights, the person said.
An explosives detection dog and a diver searched the Panama-flagged Crown Iris cruise ship on the Greek island of Syros after an unknown person said an explosive device had been attached to the boat’s hull, authorities said. Initial checks found no explosive device with coast guard specialists expected to carry out further inspections before the ship could resume its voyage.
Meanwhile, Czech public media workers went on a one-day strike to protest a government plan to overhaul how public broadcasters are funded. The legislation, led by populist billionaire turned prime minister Andrej Babiš, has been criticised as threatening the independence of the media organisations.
Russia bombarded Ukraine’s energy infrastructure in waves on Tuesday, knocking out power to swathes of the country with dozens of missiles and hundreds of drones, a week before US-brokered peace talks were due to resume.
At a press conference in Berlin with German chancellor Friedrich Merz, Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the attack showed that Moscow was intent on killing people instead of building on the humanitarian ceasefire in and around Oleshky.
Merz warned thatthe outcome of the war in Ukraine “will determine European security for a long time to come.” He said Germany will be coordinating with France and the UK, and will host a meeting of the Coalition of the Willing in Berlin later this month.
The European Commission will host a meeting regarding Ukraine with representatives from the United States, Ukraine and its key European allies on Wednesday, Commission spokesperson Paula Pinho said. “So tomorrow the European Commission will host a meeting with representatives from Ukraine, from the United States, France, Germany, the UK, Nato and the World Bank and this meeting will build on earlier talks that took place in Miami,” Pinho told reporters in Brussels.
Bomb threat prompts checks on Israel-bound cruise ship in Greek port
A bomb threat to an Israel-bound cruise ship prompted a security operation at the Greek island port of Syros after an unknown person claimed an explosive device had been attached to its hull, Greek authorities said.
The Panama-flagged Crown Iris was due to sail to Haifa carrying 940 passengers and 597 crew members when the threat was received, Reuters reported.
Coast guard personnel assisted by an explosives detection dog and a private diver searched the vessel, while a special coast guard unit was deployed to the scene.
Initial checks found no explosive device. Coast guard specialists are expected to arrive at 9.30pm (7.30pm GMT) to carry out further inspections before the ship can resume its voyage.
Czech public media workers strike over government plan to overhaul funding
Here are some images from earlier today as Czech public media workers went on a one-day strike to protest a government plan to overhaul how public broadcasters are funded.
The legislation, led by populist billionaire turned prime minister Andrej Babiš, has been criticised as threatening the independence of the media organisations. The plan led to street protests in Prague last month.
Under the plan, the country’s public radio and television would be financed from the state budget, not from an existing system of regular fees from individuals, households and businesses. The media would receive about 15% less money than they do now, which could likely lead to staff layoffs, limited production and program cancellations.
Critics say the overhaul would give the ruling three-party coalition the means to take control of the media, similar to what populist governments did in Slovakia under prime minister Robert Fico and in Hungary before former prime minister Viktor Orbán was ousted from power in April.
Michal Kubal, chief news editor at Czech Television, said the strike today is unprecedented in the history of Czech public service media.
On their TV screens, Czech residents on Tuesday saw an announcement saying:
We are doing everything we can to ensure that we can continue to provide a public service in its full scope and quality in the future.
The UK government confirmed that two of the planes affected had departed from British airports.
A spokesperson said:
The UK has one of the most robust aviation security systems in the world, with well-tested processes for dealing with any potential threats, as well as malicious hoax threats, like those we’ve seen today.
Our world-leading police and intelligence agencies work closely every day to keep us safe, using the tools they have to assess and respond to potential threats.
Bulgaria confirms bomb threats against flights from Bergamo, Dublin, not Israel
There is also an update from Bulgaria, with the country’s transport ministry telling Reuters the bomb threats were actually made against two planes from Bergamo in Italy and Dublin in Ireland, and not from Israel as previously reported.
That brings the total to seven planes (that we know of).
Back to Berlin, Ukraine’s Zelenskyy also rejects Russia’s suggestion of a meeting in Moscow as “counterproductive.” He says what’s needed is serious talks, and not a gimmick.
He also insists that Russia has no advantage on the frontline at the moment.
Merz then adds that the 19 November meeting will decide further support for Ukraine in 2027, and that concludes the press.
Two false bomb threats reported on Italy-bound Ryanair flights
Meanwhile, two more false bomb threats were reported in Italy involving Ryanair flights from Lisbon and Dublin to Rome’s Fiumicino Airport, according to the Italian newspapers La Repubblica and Corriere della Sera.
The plane from Dublin was escorted by two Italian air force fighter jets, newspaper reported.
In both cases, routine checks were confirmed as negative, meaning no threat was identified, SkyTG24 said.
That brings the total of flights affected by false alarms today to at least six, up from four reported earlier (that we know of).
Security guarantees, Ukraine reconstructions, energy and Black Sea truce to be discussed in Abu Dhabi, Zelenskyy says
Asked about his expectations for the Abu Dhabi talks, Zelenskyy says he hopes to see future security guarantees for Ukraine to be covered, alongside a “prosperity package” that would help with the reconstruction of Ukraine.
He also says he hopes to discuss a proposal on energy, Black Sea truce, which is “in the interest of not only Ukraine, but also Russia and various nations in Africa.”
He reiterates that “there can be no stable peace unless Europe is at the negotiating table.”
Merz for his part says that “it is crucial for Russia to finally engage in serious negotiations.”
Europe remains 'crucial' for ending the war in Ukraine, Zelenskyy says, as he confirms Abu Dhabi talks
Responding, Zelenskyy thanks Germany for its continued help, including on air defence, and says that while many people will be following the events in the US today’s midterm elections, “the role of Europe – and specifically Germany – remains crucial.”
He says he briefed Merz on the latest attacks on Ukraine.
He also confirms the upcoming Abu Dhabi talks on 10-11 November (11:21), which he says hopefully “will pave the way for a trilateral meeting at the level of heads of states and government.”
He also confirms further talks on Ukraine will be held in Brussels on Wednesday (12:41), as per the European Commission’s announcement earlier, and that the coalition of the willing will meet in Berlin on 19 November.
Merz declares Germany will keep supporting Ukraine as he warns about Russia's attacks, impact of Black Sea strikes on food security
Germany’s Merz begins by saying Zelenskyy’s visit comes “at a critical moment” as Russian attacks on Ukraine continued with “undiminished – indeed, increasing – severity and ruthlessness.”
He says Ukraine “can continue to rely on Germany,” with more support from Berlin in the coming months, including on air defence, energy, and broader winter-related aid.
Merz also warns that the outcome of the war in Ukraine “will determine European security for a long time to come.”
He says Germany will be coordinating with France and the UK, and will host a meeting of the Coalition of the Willing in Berlin later this month.
The German chancellor also talks of growing concerns about the broader effects of the continuing war, including a potential “global food crisis” triggered by Russia’s continued attacks on trading routes in the Black Sea.
He says the upcoming Abu Dhabi talks are “the right step forward,” and Europe hopes to play its part.
In the meantime, Berlin and partners will “increase the pressure on Moscow and continue to support Ukraine,” he says.

Under the plan, the country’s public radio and television would be financed from the state budget, not from an existing system of regular fees from individuals, households and businesses. The media would receive about 15% less money than they do now, which could likely lead to staff layoffs, limited production and program cancellations.
Critics say the overhaul would give the ruling three-party coalition the means to take control of the media, similar to what populist governments did in Slovakia under prime minister Robert Fico and in Hungary before former prime minister Viktor Orbán was ousted from power in April.
Michal Kubal, chief news editor at Czech Television, said the strike today is unprecedented in the history of Czech public service media.
On their TV screens, Czech residents on Tuesday saw an announcement saying:
We are doing everything we can to ensure that we can continue to provide a public service in its full scope and quality in the future.
The UK government confirmed that two of the planes affected had departed from British airports.
A spokesperson said:
The UK has one of the most robust aviation security systems in the world, with well-tested processes for dealing with any potential threats, as well as malicious hoax threats, like those we’ve seen today.
Our world-leading police and intelligence agencies work closely every day to keep us safe, using the tools they have to assess and respond to potential threats.
Bulgaria confirms bomb threats against flights from Bergamo, Dublin, not Israel
There is also an update from Bulgaria, with the country’s transport ministry telling Reuters the bomb threats were actually made against two planes from Bergamo in Italy and Dublin in Ireland, and not from Israel as previously reported.
That brings the total to seven planes (that we know of).
Back to Berlin, Ukraine’s Zelenskyy also rejects Russia’s suggestion of a meeting in Moscow as “counterproductive.” He says what’s needed is serious talks, and not a gimmick.
He also insists that Russia has no advantage on the frontline at the moment.
Merz then adds that the 19 November meeting will decide further support for Ukraine in 2027, and that concludes the press.
Two false bomb threats reported on Italy-bound Ryanair flights
Meanwhile, two more false bomb threats were reported in Italy involving Ryanair flights from Lisbon and Dublin to Rome’s Fiumicino Airport, according to the Italian newspapers La Repubblica and Corriere della Sera.
The plane from Dublin was escorted by two Italian air force fighter jets, newspaper reported.
In both cases, routine checks were confirmed as negative, meaning no threat was identified, SkyTG24 said.
That brings the total of flights affected by false alarms today to at least six, up from four reported earlier (that we know of).
Security guarantees, Ukraine reconstructions, energy and Black Sea truce to be discussed in Abu Dhabi, Zelenskyy says
Asked about his expectations for the Abu Dhabi talks, Zelenskyy says he hopes to see future security guarantees for Ukraine to be covered, alongside a “prosperity package” that would help with the reconstruction of Ukraine.
He also says he hopes to discuss a proposal on energy, Black Sea truce, which is “in the interest of not only Ukraine, but also Russia and various nations in Africa.”
He reiterates that “there can be no stable peace unless Europe is at the negotiating table.”
Merz for his part says that “it is crucial for Russia to finally engage in serious negotiations.”
Europe remains 'crucial' for ending the war in Ukraine, Zelenskyy says, as he confirms Abu Dhabi talks
Responding, Zelenskyy thanks Germany for its continued help, including on air defence, and says that while many people will be following the events in the US today’s midterm elections, “the role of Europe – and specifically Germany – remains crucial.”
He says he briefed Merz on the latest attacks on Ukraine.
He also confirms the upcoming Abu Dhabi talks on 10-11 November (11:21), which he says hopefully “will pave the way for a trilateral meeting at the level of heads of states and government.”
He also confirms further talks on Ukraine will be held in Brussels on Wednesday (12:41), as per the European Commission’s announcement earlier, and that the coalition of the willing will meet in Berlin on 19 November.
Merz declares Germany will keep supporting Ukraine as he warns about Russia's attacks, impact of Black Sea strikes on food security
Germany’s Merz begins by saying Zelenskyy’s visit comes “at a critical moment” as Russian attacks on Ukraine continued with “undiminished – indeed, increasing – severity and ruthlessness.”
He says Ukraine “can continue to rely on Germany,” with more support from Berlin in the coming months, including on air defence, energy, and broader winter-related aid.
Merz also warns that the outcome of the war in Ukraine “will determine European security for a long time to come.”
He says Germany will be coordinating with France and the UK, and will host a meeting of the Coalition of the Willing in Berlin later this month.
The German chancellor also talks of growing concerns about the broader effects of the continuing war, including a potential “global food crisis” triggered by Russia’s continued attacks on trading routes in the Black Sea.
He says the upcoming Abu Dhabi talks are “the right step forward,” and Europe hopes to play its part.
In the meantime, Berlin and partners will “increase the pressure on Moscow and continue to support Ukraine,” he says.

title: From the US midterms to the hard right in Britain, empathy has become a dirty word in politics | John Harris
content_c:
Towards the end of the summer, the Tory-Reform defector Robert Jenrick authored an op-ed piece for the Daily Telegraph about the seemingly impossible economics of rising benefits bills because of mental ill-health. In his capacity as Reform’s Treasury spokesman, his task was to big up its plans to cut 25% of so-called welfare spending by 2030, and thereby tackle what he called the state’s “suicidal empathy”.
Straight away, I wondered where this most opportunistic politician had borrowed that phrase from, and instantly found out: a book with the same title, published this year by the Canadian academic Gad Saad, whom the dust jacket describes as having particular expertise in “the use of evolutionary psychology in marketing and consumer behaviour”. It comes with an endorsement from Elon Musk. “Western civilisation is doomed unless the core weakness of suicidal empathy is recognised and actions are taken that are hard but necessary for survival,” says the world’s richest man. “All of Gad’s books, including this one, are great.”
Unfortunately, Suicidal Empathy is not great. It is, in fact, a baggy mess, glueing together absurd straw men (“suicidal empathy can cause people to care more about rapists and other felons than their victims”) to familiar arguments about immigration, Covid lockdowns and whether the word “imbecile” is offensive. One of its most head-turning claims is that the west’s supposed embrace of degenerate woke-ism is largely traceable to the fact that “women are much more likely to succumb to such emotional and ideological capture”. At a push, its most useful function is as a meandering guide to the soup of ideas simmering in the minds of hardcore Maga voters as they prepared for this week’s midterms.
There is a huge amount of this stuff around, crystallising the philosophical core of Trumpism and its adherent movements across the world – roughly, the idea that might is right and compassion is for wimps. We are now well beyond the culture wars and the US right’s long history of (to put it politely) Christian revisionism, and into the very serious prospect of a decisive western moral counter-revolution that may already be under way. That’s certainly the intention of the slew of voices responsible for podcasts, social media posts and other Maga potboilers – witness 2024’s Toxic Empathy: How Progressives Exploit Christian Compassion, by the Christian podcaster Allie Beth Stuckey, or last year’s The Sin of Empathy: Compassion and its Counterfeits, by the rightwing pastor Joe Rigney.
But here’s the crucial thing: the same moral push is also supported by alarming numbers of regular people. According to polling by the Public Religion Research Institute, while 84% of registered US Democrats support the proposition that empathy helps build a healthy society, only 54% of Republicans agree. Perhaps most strikingly, to quote from the survey’s accompanying blurb: “White evangelical Protestants are the only religious group in which a majority does not agree that empathy is a foundational moral value (42%). Instead, a majority (54%) say empathy can be dangerous.”
Much the same seems to be true of that possible Trump successor, JD Vance – a Catholic convert who now has the rare distinction of having locked horns with two popes. In April, Leo XIV plainly decried the US’s attacks on Iran, insisting: “Anyone who is a disciple of Christ, the Prince of Peace, is never on the side of those who once wielded the sword and today drop bombs.” Vance’s response? “I think it’s very, very important for the pope to be careful when he talks about matters of theology.” Only a few months before, the vice-president insisted his “old-school” notion of Christian compassion descended in priority from “your family”, “your neighbor” and “your community” to “your fellow citizens in your own country”. Then and only then, he said, could you “focus [sic] and prioritize the rest of the world”.
Soon after, our era’s most pre-eminent moral philosopher was interviewed by the podcaster Joe Rogan. “The fundamental weakness of western civilisation,” said Musk, “is empathy, the empathy exploit.” Progressives, he said, have set themselves on “exploiting a bug in western civilisation, which is the empathy response”.
At that point, I went straight back to one of my favourite modern books: the classicist and historian Tom Holland’s bestseller Dominion, that brilliant history of Christianity and its global impact that illuminates how an emphasis on what we now call empathy (the word was only created in 1908, as the English translation of the German “Einfühlung”, or “in-feeling”) was one of that religion’s philosophical revolutions.
“Across the Roman world,” Holland writes, “wailing at the sides of roads or on rubbish tips, babies abandoned by their parents were a common sight.” Such everyday barbarism was also reflected in official attitudes to poor, disabled and infirm people – until a moral up-ending began with Rome’s conversion to Christianity under Constantine. As Holland writes: “Every week in churches across the Roman world, collections for orphans and widows, for the imprisoned, and the shipwrecked and the sick had been raised … Entire systems of social security had begun to emerge.” But there was an additional element of this sea change – which, in a modern context, stands in sharp contrast to everything from ICE detention camps to Musk’s vandalism of USAID and the 700,000 deaths it is reckoned to have already caused. As Holland puts it, “divine love for the outcast and derelict demanded that mortals love them too”.
No one would claim Christian countries and institutions stuck to those ideas in the centuries that followed, but the modern US is surely now moral light years away. And there is a British story here, too, bound up with the changes brought to our politics by Margaret Thatcher – who was raised as a strict Methodist, and occasionally blurted out quite remarkable opinions about Christian teaching and questions of morality: in January 1980, for example, she claimed that “no one would remember the Good Samaritan if he’d only had good intentions; he had money as well”.
In this and so many other respects, she was way ahead of her time, opening the path to the kind of moral contortions we hear not just from Jenrick, but both his new comrades in Reform and his former Tory colleagues. Some have gone even further: let migrants drown, they say, while others accuse the lifeboat service – the lifeboat service! – of complicity in a supposed invasion of untouchables, barely pausing for breath before they mourn the decline of “Judeo-Christian culture”. In the States, a proper Republican drubbing on Tuesday might give the anti-empaths the kind of shock they deserve, but Musk’s power and influence alone shows that it will take a lot more than a single round of election results to really push them back. Meanwhile, all over the world, compassion, kindness and other such virtues gather a thick layer of dust, like old hymn books in a long-deserted church.
- 
  John Harris is a Guardian columnist

title: What US midterm elections mean for Ukraine, Iran and elsewhere
content_c:
What US midterm elections mean for Ukraine, Iran and elsewhere
November 3, 2026
The outcome of the midterm elections will shape US policy for years — and have repercussions around the globe. Decisions made in Washington affect both US adversaries such as Iran and countries such as Ukraine, which is seeking more support from the United States.
President Donald Trump does not have the final say when it comes to deciding where the United States goes to war or which countries get financial or military aid. While the president wields more power in the US than in parliamentary democracies such as Germany, he does not govern alone — even in the land of opportunity.
The House of Representatives and the Senate, the two chambers of Congress whose composition voters will decide this Tuesday, wield considerable influence. They decide on legislation and government spending and also serve as a check on the president and the intelligence agencies.
The president can veto legislation passed by Congress. Congress can override that veto with a two-thirds majority in both chambers. The legislature also handles impeachment proceedings. In addition, the president can only appoint Cabinet members, US ambassadors and federal judges from a list of nominees the Senate approves.
Trump’s Republicans currently hold majorities in both chambers of Congress, making it easier for the president to govern. But recent polls suggest the Democrats could take control of at least the House of Representatives and possibly even the Senate. This could shift the direction of major foreign policy issues.
Support for Ukraine
Joe Biden, a Democrat, was in the White House when Russia launched its invasion of Ukraine. Alongside Europe, the US stood out as a reliable partner, supporting Ukraine with financial aid, military expertise and, above all, large-scale weapons deliveries.
The situation changed abruptly under Trump. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy famously received a notably frosty welcome during his 2025 visit to the White House. Trump now openly admits that he gets along better with Russian President Vladimir Putin than with Zelenskyy.
The US has suspended sanctions against Russia and reduced financial and military aid to Ukraine. If Democrats win majorities in both chambers of Congress, they could put increased support for Ukraine on the agenda.
"Democrats criticize the Trump administration for not doing enough for Ukraine," Brandon Conradis, a former DW journalist and now an editor at Bloomberg Government, told DW. "They can push legislation that would provide more aid to Ukraine."
If Trump vetoed such legislation, the outcome would depend on the balance of power in Congress. But a two-thirds majority could override his veto with support from some Republicans.
Iran War
Trump launched the war against Iran alongside Israel on February 28 without consulting Congress. Under the US Constitution, Congress must approve a formal declaration of war against another country. Democrats have repeatedly voted against the war and even passed a resolution, together with some Republicans, calling for an end to the hostilities. The Trump administration has ignored it.
"I don't think Congress will have huge powers here," said Michael O'Hanlon, director of research for foreign policy at the US think tank Brookings Institution, told DW, but added that Congress could perhaps prevent a major escalation by refusing to fund it.
How the midterms could impact development aid
US support for aid projects around the world that help fight Ebola, AIDS and hunger was sharply cut back by President Trump shortly after he began his second term. Among other measures, he shut down USAID, the US agency responsible for foreign development assistance.
Whether a Democratic-controlled Congress could "reactivate" the agency against the president's wishes is questionable. But Congress could push for increased aid spending and investigate the controversial closure of USAID.
"Democrats would have oversight power and use it to scrutinize the closing of USAID," Conradis said. "There will be hearings, and they will drag officials they view as responsible in front of Congress."
Ultimately, the US remains a country with a Republican president. There will be no complete reversal of course. "It's not like if Democrats win control of Congress, everything is going to change. But some things will change because the power dynamics will be different."
This article was originally published in German.
description: Donald Trump's Republicans control the US Congress, but that could change after the midterm elections. The outcome of the ballot will not only impact domestic policy but also conflicts in Europe and the Middle East.

title: Chile: Gericht entscheidet im Sorgerechtsstreit um Katze »Perseo«
content_c:
Sorgerechtsstreit über Haustier Oberstes Gericht in Chile urteilt, dass monatliches Pendeln für Katze unzumutbar ist
In Chile hat der oberste Gerichtshof in einem Rechtsstreit über eine Katze geurteilt, dass monatliches Pendeln zwischen den beiden Ex-Partnern dem Tier nicht zuzumuten sei. Der Vierbeiner namens »Perseo« sei als »fühlendes Wesen« zu betrachten. Dessen Wohlergehen müsse Vorrang vor den Interessen und Rechten seiner Besitzer haben, begründeten die Richter ihren einstimmigen Beschluss.
Behalten Sie den Überblick: Jeden Werktag gegen 18 Uhr beantworten SPIEGEL-Autorinnen und -Autoren die wichtigsten Fragen des Tages im Newsletter »Die Lage am Abend« – hintergründig, kompakt, kostenlos. Hier bestellen Sie Ihr News-Briefing als Mail.
Nach dem Bürgerlichen Gesetzbuch Chiles gelten Tiere zwar als »bewegliche Sachen im Sinne des gemeinschaftlichen Eigentumsrechts«. Doch die fünf Richterinnen und Richter der höchsten Instanz bewerteten den Schutz der Katze nun höher (hier die Entscheidung im Original). In lokalen Medien ist von einem »beispiellosen Präzedenzfall im Bereich des Tierschutzes« die Rede.
Konkret sprach das oberste Gericht der Frau des einstigen Paares das Recht zu, die Katze zu betreuen. Damit bestätigte es ein Urteil des zweitinstanzlichen Berufungsgerichtes von Valdivia.
Der Ex-Partner hatte den exklusiven Besitz der Frau an »Perseo« beanstandet und stattdessen eine abwechselnde Betreuung des Haustiers gefordert. Das Tier hatten sich der Mann und die Frau Berichten zufolge im Jahr 2021 angeschafft, als sie noch ein Paar waren. Nach der Trennung verklagte der Mann dann seine Ex-Partnerin.

Suche erfolgreich: Entlaufene Katze nach fast einem Monat an Autobahnraststätte wiedergefunden1 Min1 Min
In erster Instanz hatte er noch gewonnen und ein geteiltes Sorgerecht für die Katze erstritten. Die monatliche Übergabe des Tieres sollte laut Medienberichten auf einer Polizeiwache erfolgen. Die Frau ging gegen diese Regelung in Berufung und gewann. Dagegen ging wiederum der Mann vor – und der Fall landete vor dem obersten Gericht.
Die Richterinnen und Richter vertraten dort nun die Ansicht, dass das Miteigentum nicht ausschlaggebend sei. Zudem würde die »hohe Konfliktbereitschaft der Parteien es ausschließen, dass das Wohlergehen der Hauskatze im Rahmen eines gemeinsamen Sorgerechts gewährleistet werden könnte«.
description: Was passiert mit dem gemeinsamen Haustier, wenn ein Paar sich trennt? Mit dieser Frage musste sich jetzt in Chile der oberste Gerichtshof befassen. Es entschied: Das Wohl der Katze ist wichtiger als die Interessen der Besitzer.

title: Weitere gefährliche Halloween-Süßigkeiten entdeckt - auch im Ausland
content_c:
Fälle auch im Ausland Weitere gefährliche Halloween-Süßigkeiten entdeckt
Nadeln in Schokoriegeln, Metall in Fruchtgummi: Immer mehr manipulierte Halloween-Süßigkeiten werden gemeldet - und das nicht nur in Deutschland. In einigen Fällen verletzten sich Kinder.
Nach Halloween sind weitere Fälle von Süßigkeiten bekannt geworden, in denen sich Nadeln, Schrauben oder andere Metallgegenstände befanden. Entsprechende Meldungen über solche Funde gab es in mehreren Bundesländern.
So entdeckte in Duderstadt in Niedersachen eine Elfjährige einen mit einer Nadel gespickten Schokoriegel und in Höxter, Nordrhein-Westfalen, bemerkte ein Vater ein Metallstück in einem Eiskonfekt. Im niederbayerischen Pilsting wurde eine Nadel in einer Süßigkeit sowie ein drahtähnlicher Gegenstand gefunden. In Unterfranken meldete die Polizei gleich drei neue Funde: In zwei Schokoriegeln steckten Nadeln, in einem Fruchtgummi ein scharfkantiges Metallteil.
Vorläufigen Zahlen der bayerischen Polizei zufolge sind im Freistaat zu Halloween deutlich mehr mit gefährlichen Gegenständen gespickte Süßigkeiten entdeckt worden als im Vorjahr. Eine Recherche im Vorgangsverwaltungssystem der Polizei habe für das laufende Jahr 25 Fälle von Süßigkeiten mit Nadeln, Schrauben und Nägeln ergeben, teilte das bayerische Landeskriminalamt (LKA) mit. Andere Gegenstände seien nicht abgefragt worden, die Dunkelziffer könne also noch deutlich höher sein.
Kinder durch Nadeln leicht verletzt
Durch eine versteckte Nadel zog sich ein Kind aus Neustadt-Glewe im Kreis Ludwigslust-Parchim leichte Verletzungen im Mundbereich zu, wie die Polizei mitteilte. Im niedersächsischen Bremervörde verletzte sich eine Neunjährige an einer fünf Zentimeter langen Stecknadel in einem Schokoriegel an der Zunge.
Die Polizei rief alle Eltern dazu auf, die Süßigkeiten der Kinder zu überprüfen und verdächtige Fälle zu melden. Mit Blick auf den Martinstag am 11. November mahnte die Polizei Düsseldorf zudem zu besonderer Vorsicht. "Wir können nicht ausschließen, dass sich manche Menschen als Trittbrettfahrer betätigen und sich einen vermeintlichen Spaß machen wollen", sagte eine Sprecherin.
Funde in mehreren europäischen Ländern
Nicht nur in Deutschland wurden Funde von präparierten Süßigkeiten bekannt - auch in Österreich meldete in mehreren Bundesländern kleine Metallobjekte in Süßigkeiten. Ein Mädchen verletzte sich laut österreichischen Behörden leicht.
Auf einer Pressekonferenz sagte der Österreichs Innenminister Gerhard Karner: "Wir werden alles Menschenmögliche tun, damit wir dieses feige und hinterhältige Verbrechen aufklären." Als Konsequenz wurde im Bundeskriminalamt in Wien eine Ermittlungseinheit eingesetzt. Sie soll auch den Kontakt zu deutschen Behörden und Europol herstellen.
Aus weitere Ländern gab es ähnliche Berichte über manipulierte Süßigkeiten. In Norwegen fand ein 13-jähriges Mädchen eine Nadel in einer Lakritzstange, ein weiteres Mädchen entdeckte eine Nadel in einem Schokoriegel. In Irland wurden kleine Metallnadeln in Süßigkeiten in mindestens drei Städten gefunden. In Dänemark gab es im Großraum Kopenhagen einzelne Fälle. Auch Ungarn soll betroffen sein.
Diese manipulierten Süßigkeiten wurden im österreichischen Bundesland Steiermark gefunden.
Waren Täter online vernetzt?
Gerald Tatzgern, Abteilungsleiter für Ermittlungen im österreichischen Bundeskriminalamt, sagte: Es könne nicht ausgeschlossen werden, dass die Täter im Internet, in sozialen Medien oder in Online-Foren vernetzt gewesen seien.
In Deutschland teilte das Landesinnenministerium Rheinland-Pfalz mit, dass bisher noch keine Erkenntnisse vorliegen, welche "auf eine systematische oder landesweit koordinierte Vorgehensweise schließen lassen".
Europol erklärte gegenüber der Nachrichtenagentur dpa, dass man die nationalen Behörden bei der Aufklärung unterstützen werde, jedoch keine eigene Taskforce einrichten wolle.

title: Frankfurt-Krawalle: Generalverdacht gegen Migranten?
content_c:
Frankfurt-Krawalle: Generalverdacht gegen Migranten?
3. November 2026
Es waren Straßenschlachten, die sich am Samstag (31.10.) in der Innenstadt von Frankfurt am Main bis tief in die Nacht zogen. Polizisten, Feuerwehr- und Rettungskräfte wurden mit Steinen, Flaschen und Brandsätzen beworfen, Geschäfte wurden beschädigt und geplündert. Am Ende waren mehr als 100 Polizisten verletzt, einer davon schwer.
Auch in Köln, Hamburg und Berlin eskalierte die Lage, nachdem zuvor bundesweit zehntausende junge Menschen überwiegend friedlich auf die Straße gegangen waren. Die Initiative "Gen Z regelt" hatte dazu aufgerufen, um auf die Zukunftssorgen der jungen Generation aufmerksam zu machen und unter anderem für bessere Bildungschancen, bezahlbaren Wohnraum und mehr Klimaschutz zu demonstrieren.
Frankfurt-Krawalle: Politik streitet über Ursachen und Verantwortung
Nach den Ausschreitungen setzten Bundesinnenminister Alexander Dobrindt (CSU) und der hessische Innenminister Roman Poseck (CDU) schnell den Ton. Die meisten der Festgenommenen hätten die deutsche Staatsangehörigkeit, sagte Poseck, fügte aber hinzu: "Diese Tätergruppe war überwiegend migrantisch geprägt." Dobrindt sagte: "Es gab friedliche Demonstrationen, die dann Richtung Abend gekapert worden sind von gewaltbereiten linken Gruppen und migrantischen Chaoten." Damit fachten die beiden konservativen Politiker eine politische Debatte an, die nachhallt.
Es geht um Gewalt und Strafverfolgung. Aber auch um Migration, Integration und die Frage, ob bei Enkeln und Urenkeln von Zuwanderern immer noch davon gesprochen wird, dass diese Menschen einen Migrationshintergrund haben. Dazu kommt die Frage, ob Begriffe wie "migrantische Chaoten" Probleme benennen oder Vorurteile verstärken. Die Zukunftsängste der "Gen Z" drohen dahinter zu verblassen.
Migration, Integration und die Frage nach dem Tätermilieu
Bundeskanzler Friedrich Merz (CDU) stellte sich ausdrücklich hinter die Äußerungen seines Innenministers. Dessen Einschätzung zum Tätermilieu speise sich "aus den Beobachtungen der Ermittlungsbehörden und der Einsatzkräfte vor Ort", sagte sein Sprecher Stefan Kornelius. Sie decke sich auch "mit dem Bildmaterial, das viele gesehen haben".
Am Montagabend kündigte Merz ein hartes Vorgehen gegen die Randalierer an. "Gewalt hat auf unseren Straßen nichts zu suchen, und meine Regierung wird hier keine Toleranz zeigen", sagte Merz laut Redemanuskript auf einer parteiinternen Veranstaltung der CDU in Berlin. "Wer Polizisten und Einsatzkräfte angreift und Geschäfte plündert, greift unsere Freiheit an, verhöhnt die Gesellschaft und die berechtigten Interessen der jungen Leute."
Regierung kündigt harte Strafen für Gewalttäter an
Die Sozialdemokraten, die mit den konservativen Parteien CDU/CSU die Bundesregierung bilden, stimmen in diesem Punkt durchaus zu. Klar sei, dass es sich um Straftäter handle, sagte SPD-Bundesverteidigungsminister Boris Pistorius am Sonntagabend im ZDF. "Es sind Kriminelle, die Polizisten angreifen und verletzen, schwere Sachbeschädigungen begehen."
Damit aber enden die Gemeinsamkeiten. "Was sind denn migrantische Gruppen?", entgegnete Pistorius auf die Wortwahl des Bundesinnenministers. "Sind das Menschen, die in dritter Generation in Deutschland leben und deutsche Staatsangehörige sind? Wo hören wir auf, das zu differenzieren?", wandte er ein. "Ich glaube, das führt in die falsche Richtung."
SPD warnt vor pauschalen Zuschreibungen
Die Integrationsbeauftragte der Bundesregierung, die SPD-Politikerin Natalie Pawlik, legte am Montag nach. "Solche Gewaltausschreitungen immer gleich migrantischen Milieus zuzuschreiben, ist zu einfach", sagte Pawlik der "Frankfurter Allgemeinen Zeitung" in einem Interview. "Denn pauschale Gruppenzuschreibungen treffen auch diejenigen mit Einwanderungsgeschichte, die friedlich demonstriert haben oder selbst als Einsatzkräfte bei Polizei oder Rettungsdienst im Einsatz waren."
Die Gewaltausschreitungen seien durch nichts zu rechtfertigen und müssten konsequent bestraft werden. Doch wenn die Ermittlungen zeigten, dass bestimmte Gruppen besonders beteiligt gewesen seien, dann müssten vor allem auch die Ursachen für die Gewalttaten benannt werden. "Dabei dürfen auch schwierige Fragen nach fehlenden Perspektiven, Ausgrenzungserfahrungen oder möglichen Integrationsproblemen nicht ausgeklammert werden", sagte Pawlik.
Ursachen der Gewalt: Fehlende Perspektiven im Fokus
Auf die Ursachen will auch Bundesfamilien- und Bildungsministerin Karin Prien (CDU) schauen. Es gehe nicht darum, Ressentiments zu schüren, sagte sie im Deutschlandfunk. "Das wäre auch politisch falsch." Es gehe vielmehr darum, die Realität zu betrachten. "Wenn die (Täter) aus migrantischen Milieus stammen, dann muss uns das Sorgen bereiten", sagte Prien.
Laut Statistischem Bundesamt haben rund 31 Prozent der deutschen Bevölkerung einen Migrationshintergrund. Höher liegt er in mehreren großen Städten. In Frankfurt am Main hat mehr als jeder zweite Einwohner eine Zuwanderungsgeschichte. Laut Prien müsse gefragt werden, warum Integration in manchen Zuwanderungsgruppen weniger gelinge als in anderen. Die eigentliche Herausforderung bestehe darin, gesellschaftliche Teilhabe zu ermöglichen und Parallelwelten zu verhindern.
Gen-Z-Proteste: Streit über Demonstrationsrecht und Konsequenzen
Die politische Diskussion wird dadurch verschärft, dass der hessische Innenminister inzwischen ein Verbot weiterer "Gen-Z-Proteste" ins Spiel gebracht hat. Mit Blick auf angekündigte Demonstrationen am 20. November sagte Poseck, das Versammlungsrecht sei zwar ein hohes Gut. "Die Friedlichkeit" sei jedoch ebenso elementar. Aus seiner Sicht gab es bereits während der Demonstrationen "massive Angriffe" auf die Polizei. "Die Versammlungsleiter haben diese Versammlungen nicht im Griff."
Die Organisatoren der Demonstrationen weisen die Vorwürfe zurück. Sie hatten sich umgehend von den Ausschreitungen distanziert. Das Bundesfamilienministerium kündigte nun an, dass sich Ministerin Prien noch in dieser Woche mit Vertreterinnen und Vertretern der Bundesschülerkonferenz sowie der Gewerkschaft Erziehung und Wissenschaft (GEW) zum Austausch verabredet habe.
Prien selbst rief dazu auf, die Interessen jüngerer Menschen stärker zu berücksichtigen. "Das sind genau die Debatten, die wir jetzt führen müssen, die auch die jungen Menschen sehr zurecht einfordern", sagte sie im Sender RBB.

title: Життя зміниться вже 4 листопада: 4 знаки китайського зодіаку знайдуть те, чого їм бракувало
content_c:
Життя зміниться вже 4 листопада: 4 знаки китайського зодіаку знайдуть те, чого їм бракувало
Чотири знаки китайського зодіаку можуть нарешті забути про самотність 4 листопада 2026 року. Астрологи прогнозують їм нові знайомства, відновлення дружби та несподівані зустрічі.
У середу, 4 листопада 2026 року, чотири знаки китайського зодіаку можуть нарешті позбутися відчуття самотності. День успіху Водяного Коня сприятиме новим знайомствам, відновленню дружби та пошуку людей, які здатні зрозуміти й підтримати.
Про це повідомило видання Yourtango.
За астрологічним прогнозом, енергія цього дня особливо гармонійно поєднуватиметься зі стихією Вогняного Коня, яка панує 2026 року. Для деяких знаків це стане нагодою вийти зі звичного усамітнення та повернути спілкування у своє життя.
- Щур
Представники цього знака останнім часом могли відчувати, що саме вони постійно підтримують зв’язок з іншими, тоді як близькі рідко виявляють ініціативу. Через це виникало відчуття, що їх недостатньо цінують.
Однак 4 листопада ситуація може змінитися. Щури вирішать частіше бувати серед людей і відкриються до нових знайомств. Випадкова зустріч із незнайомцем може перерости в напрочуд приємну розмову, яка нагадає, наскільки важливе взаємне зацікавлення.

Дракони пережили непростий період, протягом якого їм бракувало розуміння навіть від найближчого оточення. Вони потребували не стільки порад, скільки людей, здатних розділити їхні переживання.
У середу представники знака можуть знайти таку підтримку в інтернет-спільноті. Спілкування з тими, хто зіткнувся зі схожими труднощами, допоможе їм відчути, що вони більше не залишаються наодинці зі своїми проблемами.

Представники знака можуть несподівано виявити спільний інтерес із людиною, яку давно знають. Це допоможе їм краще зрозуміти одне одного та повернути щирість у стосунки. Відчуття віддаленості поступово поступиться місцем близькості, якої так бракувало.
Нагадаємо, астрологи попередили, що 4 листопада 2026 року — день, коли нам не захочеться працювати й досягати результатів — як професійних, так і фінансових, — лінощі і апатія візьмуть гору.
Астрологія, тарологія, нумерологія, ворожіння, пророцтво, мольфарство, екстрасенсорика не є науками і передбачення не завжди збуваються на 100%. Інформація досить часто має розважальний характер, тому сприймати її потрібно не серйозно, а лише як ймовірність подій, творцем яких може стати кожна людина, якщо матиме сили духу та натхнення змінити своє життя на краще.

title: ПСЖ и Ямаль отметились новыми рекордами в Лиге чемпионов
content_c:
В рамках игрового дня 3 ноября в Лиге чемпионов был установлен ряд рекордов. На турнире начались поединки четвертого тура.
Действующий победитель ЛЧ "Пари Сен-Жермен" гостил у "Вильярреала" в Испании и одержал победу со счетом 6:0, а всю игру в составе парижан на поле провел украинский защитник Илья Забарный.
При этом ПСЖ установил рекорд. Команда Луиса Энрике забила четыре гола всего за 16 минут и 2 секунды после стартового свистка усилиями Жоау Невеша (9 минута), Дезире Дуэ (12), Сенни Меюлю (13) и Фабиана Руиса (17).
Парижане четырежды поразили ворота соперника быстрее всех участников ЛЧ за всю историю, передает Opta. Предыдущий рекорд принадлежал мадридскому "Реалу", которому для четырех голов в матче с загребским "Динамо" в 2011 году потребовалось 20 минут.
Еще одним рекордсменом стал вингер "Барселоны" Ламин Ямаль, сообщает Squawka. 19-летний вундеркинд в матче с "Астон Виллой" (3:0) открыл счет на седьмой минуте.
Испанский футболист забил свой 14-й гол в карьере в рамках Лиги чемпионов. Он стал рекордсменом по этому показателю среди всех футболистов в возрасте до 20 лет. Ямаль обошел форварда "Реала" Килиана Мбаппе, который до своего 20-летия забил на турнире 13 голов.
Ранее сообщалось о том, что "Шахтер" потерпел второе подряд поражение в Лиге чемпионов.

title: Tenerife striker De Miguel dies after on-field collision
content_c:
Tenerife striker De Miguel dies after on-field collision
- Published
Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel has died after the 30-year-old suffered a serious injury during a Spanish second-division match.
The forward suffered head and chest injuries during a match against FC Andorra on Monday in a heavy collision with goalkeeper Jesus Owono, who was sent off for his challenge.
De Miguel's condition was described as 'stable but serious' on Monday but his health deteriorated on Tuesday morning, with the Spaniard dying at 07:00 GMT.
Reuters reported on Tuesday that police in Spain have opened an investigation for possible involuntary manslaughter following De Miguel's death.
Under Spanish law, any death that is deemed non-natural automatically triggers a judicial inquiry.
"Heartbroken, with a lump in our throats and unable to believe this is true" Tenerife said.
"There are no words of comfort; there is absolutely nothing that can lessen this overwhelming sadness. We stand with his grieving family, with his loved ones, with all of Tenerife who mourn this cruel loss today."
'There are no words'
Tenerife and Andorra were drawing 2-2 seven minutes into stoppage time when the incident occurred.
Owono ran towards the centre circle to clear a long ball when his knee appeared to collide with De Miguel.
The striker lay motionless on the pitch as medical staff treated him before he was taken by ambulance from Tenerife's Estadio Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez to hospital.
Players from both teams were visibly distressed by the incident, with a number of De Miguel's team-mates in tears.
The referee showed Owono a straight red card before abandoning the match.
The goalkeeper, who had over 30,000 followers on Instagram on Tuesday morning, has since deactivated his account.
Spanish media, including Marca, reported De Miguel suffered a cardiac arrest in the ambulance and was resuscitated by paramedics on the way to hospital.
Tenerife's president, Felipe Minambres, says the club's players will need "professional assistance" to help deal with the ordeal of one of their team-mates dying.
"We are all feeling vulnerable and deeply saddened right now. It's hard to even believe what has happened," said Minambres.
"We know, especially the players and the players' partners, that we will need support. We've already begun receiving offers of help today, and that support will continue.
"We will need professional assistance, but we also need the support of all our fans, because they are likely feeling the same way we are today."
Minambres added it had been a "truly unbelievable situation" and "an enormous tragedy that we have had to endure".
Andorra, Tenerife's opponents on Monday, issued a statement later on Tuesday which spoke of the club's shock and expressed condolences to De Miguel's family, club "and all those who were close to him".
"We are deeply affected by what has happened and we share the pain that the club is experiencing," it continued.
"From the very beginning we have maintained contact with them and we are at their disposal for anything they may need.
"What has happened has had a huge emotional impact on our players, the coaching staff and everyone at FC Andorra. These are particularly difficult times for everyone and we want to make sure that no one has to face them alone. That is why the club is providing psychological support to anyone who needs it."
Former Barcelona defender Gerard Pique, who co-owns Andorra, said: "I am sorry with all my soul. Rest in peace, Jesus."
De Miguel's former club, Castellon, said: "It's hard to find words when reality strikes in such an unfair way.
"We join with all our affection in the grief of his family and loved ones, whom we embrace in these terribly difficult moments and to whom we extend our most heartfelt condolences."
Javier Tebas, president of La Liga, said: "Today, we all share the terrible pain of an irreparable loss.
"My deepest condolences to his family, loved ones, team-mates and the whole club."
Real Madrid and France striker Kylian Mbappe wrote on his social media: "Much sadness, there are no words."
Inter Miami and former Barcelona forward Lionel Messi said: "There are no words. My condolences and lots of strength to all his family and friends."
The Spanish football federation announced following De Miguel's death that Tuesday's Spanish Cup fixtures had been postponed.
Two fixtures in the first round of the men's Copa del Rey were due to be played, while Espanyol were set to take on AS Celtas in the women's Copa del Reina competition.
A lower-league player with an eye for goal
De Miguel, who was born in Madrid, started his career at Leganes in 2015 and went on to play for eight different clubs in Spain.
After spells with Lugo Fuenlabrada and Internacional Madrid, he returned to Fuenlabrada before stints at Union Adarve, Navalcarnero and Unionistas.
He joined Castellon in 2023 and scored 16 goals as the club achieved promotion to Spain's second division a year later.
The Spaniard joined Tenerife on a three-year deal in 2025 and scored 11 goals in 29 appearances for the side.
De Miguel is survived by his daughter, Carla de Miguel Fernandez, who was born in 2025.

title: Proposal for free bus service scrapped
content_c:
Proposal for free bus service scrapped
- Published
Proposals for a free bus service in Guernsey will no longer be considered for next year's budget, deputies who suggested the move have said.
Deputies Sally Rochester and Ross Le Brun put the plan forward as an amendment to the 2027 budget, asking the Policy and Resources Committee for £1.9m to "enable the existing public transport service" to be made free of charge in a one-year pilot.
They have now pulled the plans after "concern from [operator] Stagecoach" that increased passenger numbers could mean certain routes not coping with the additional demand.
Rochester said she and Le Brun were committed to working with the Environment and Infrastructure Committee to explore plans for the future.
Rochester also acknowledged the pilot would not be possible if buses were "at capacity".
Speaking to BBC Radio Guernsey, she said: "This amendment was all about supporting those in our community that are facing cost of living challenges.
"It was about delivering the transport strategy so you could have access to a free bus service - make their lives easier, make their lives better.
"Now we're not going to be able to do that if the bus service is at capacity."
She said the "logical conclusion is that we would need more buses" while Stagecoach's contract "would need to be expanded" to provide the additional capacity.
Rochester said these elements are "what we'll be looking into and hopefully bringing this back some time in the future".
'High demand'
A spokesperson for Stagecoach said it welcomed "any initiative that encourages more people to use public transport and recognise the potential benefits of making bus travel more accessible".
But it said it was important that "any proposal to introduce free bus travel is carefully considered to ensure that sufficient capacity is available across the network to accommodate the additional passenger demand such a scheme could generate".
The company added: "Our priority is to ensure that bus services remain reliable, accessible and able to meet the needs of all passengers, particularly on routes that already experience high levels of demand."
The proposal was one of 30 changes put forward to next year's budget, scheduled for consideration on Tuesday.
Other amendments put forward include efforts to secure money for States' committees faced with budget cuts, attempts to freeze fuel duty and cuts to overseas aid.

title: Seven planes across Europe searched or diverted after ‘malicious hoax’ bomb threats
content_c:
Seven planes across Europe have been searched or diverted after a series of bomb threats were made to passenger flights, prompting questions as to whether there was any coordination behind the warnings.
Two UK departures – one from Heathrow and one from Manchester – were among those threatened in what Downing Street called “malicious hoaxes”, though all planes landed safely and no explosives were found.
A UK Department for Transport source added that the low-level threats were “not credible” and that passengers should not be concerned, though the warnings disrupted flights and prompted investigations across the UK and Europe.
None of the incidents and subsequent searches threw up any evidence of terrorist activity, though authorities were responding to an unusual number of reported threats in one day.
One of Warsaw’s two main airports, Modlin, was briefly closed after receiving a diverted plane, and Polish officials confirmed that they had received bomb threats involving two flights coming into the capital.
Italian fighter jets escorted a Ryanair plane into Rome following a warning of a suspected threat on a flight coming from Dublin. The flight landed safely and nothing untoward was reported as being found.
There was little obvious pattern surrounding the incidents, which affected flights taking off from the UK, Ireland, Denmark, Portugal and Italy, and landing in Poland, Spain, Italy and Bulgaria. Four of the flights were operated by Ryanair, the others by Wizz Air, LOT and SAS.
Investigators added there was no immediate evidence of a hostile state being behind the threats, though they continued to monitor developments, sharing information across the continent while inquiries continued.
Aviation security fears have been reignited with the recent FlyDubai incident when a co-pilot allegedly attempted to crash a Tel Aviv-bound plane. Russia has also been accused of being behind firebomb threats targeting parcel carriers using cargo planes over the past two years.
The threats followed an incident on Monday when another flight from the UK to Bulgaria was diverted, apparently without substance.
Experts said that fake threats occur on a daily basis. Philip Baum, visiting professor of aviation security at Coventry University, said: “Most are from individuals who think it is funny or want to delay a flight for some reason. If the industry was to respond to every unsubstantiated threat, flights would grind to a halt.
“The reality is that terrorist organisations who might like to smuggle a bomb on to a flight don’t tell people, they claim responsibility after the attacks.”
But he added that the fact that some aircraft did divert would “imply that the threats are credible and specific in nature, and therefore one has to respond accordingly”.
Tuesday’s series of incidents started with a flight from Heathrow operated by the Polish carrier LOT, which was scheduled to arrive at Warsaw’s Chopin airport but was diverted to the second airport, further from the Polish capital, Modlin. Authorities closed that airport after the alert and the Boeing 737 Max landed without incident.
“The passengers were evacuated and the plane underwent security checks. Nothing was found,” spokesperson Adam Szablowski told AFP. “The airport has been reopened and is operating normally.”
A Scandinavian Airlines plane from Copenhagen to Warsaw was also the subject of a threat but landed at Chopin airport, where a security inspection that did not turn up any explosive devices closed part of the airport.
Another UK departure, a Ryanair plane from Manchester, was met by emergency vehicles on landing at its destination, Murcia in southern Spain, after another threat. Spanish regional authorities confirmed on social media that no explosives were found on the flight.
The Metropolitan police confirmed its aviation unit is monitoring the situation, adding no security issues were identified following threats made against flights after they had taken off.
A UK government spokesperson said of the threats to two departures from Britain: “The UK has one of the most robust aviation security systems in the world, with well-tested processes for dealing with any potential threats, as well as malicious hoax threats, like those we’ve seen today.
“Our world-leading police and intelligence agencies work closely every day to keep us safe, using the tools they have to assess and respond to potential threats.”
In Italy, two Ryanair flights were searched at Rome’s Fiumicino airport following potential bomb threats, according to the airport operator ADR. The first was a flight from Lisbon, while a second later in the morning from Dublin was escorted in by Italian air force fighter jets until landing.
Bulgaria’s transport ministry said in a statement to Reuters that threats were made against a Wizz Air flight from Bergamo and a Ryanair flight from Dublin to the capital, Sofia. Both flights were carrying about 180 passengers and landed safely, with no devices found.
The separate incidents came the day after a Wizz Air service from London Luton made an emergency landing in Budapest, escorted by a Hungarian fighter jet.
The plane, which was due to depart from Luton at 8.15am on Monday for Sofia, was diverted after a bomb threat was received “during the flight”, Wizz Air said.
Airlines abide by a regulated process to assess and manage bomb threats, although virtually all are fake. In the UK, airlines file a mandatory occurrence report to the Civil Aviation Authority.
Ryanair did not respond to requests for comment.
